observed_behavior: Terminal SIGINT printed a Python KeyboardInterrupt traceback from the CLI wrapper while waiting on a subprocess.
expected_behavior: Cancellation exits quietly with status 130 after delegated cleanup.
causal_mechanism: The parent treated SIGINT as an uncaught Python exception independently of the child cancellation lifecycle; Python's interrupted subprocess wait could return before child cleanup finished.

anti_pattern.structural_description: A process dispatcher lacks a cancellation boundary and abandons ownership of delegated cleanup on parent interruption.
anti_pattern.why_it_fails: Foreground-group SIGINT reaches parent and child together, so the parent's exception can leak a traceback and terminate its wait while the child is still finalizing.

correct_pattern.required_invariant: The dispatcher remains responsible for waiting on the selected child's cancellation cleanup and classifies cancellation separately from ordinary failure.
correct_pattern.implementation_description: A scoped SIGINT handler records delegated cancellation without throwing through subprocess.run; built-in Python entry boundaries catch KeyboardInterrupt, shell traps preserve status 130, and ordinary errors remain visible.

applicability_conditions: Foreground terminal SIGINT reaches a Python dispatcher and its selected child.
known_non_matches: The index's existing commit checkpoint protocol already preserves completed transactions; it was not the cause of the wrapper traceback.
confirmation_evidence: Before repair, process-group SIGINT during Git discovery printed a subprocess/selectors traceback before a Node command ran.
After repair, delegated cleanup lasting 700ms completed before wrapper exit.
regression_proofs: tests/ponytail-cli.test.js: Ctrl-C is quiet in the wrapper and waits for delegated cleanup
tests/pm-pdf.test.js: ponytail pm pdf handles Ctrl-C without a Python traceback
scripts/test-project-index-postgres.sh: registered CLI SIGINT preserves checkpoints and resumes
